explanation: Write a=5λ. The general solution is y=(A+Bx)e^{ax}. For a=0, the boundary conditions force the zero solution. For a≠0, y'(1)=0 gives A=-B(1+a)/a. Then y(2)+2y'(2)=Be^{2a}(1-1/a+2a)=0, so 2a²+a-1=(2a-1)(a+1)=0. Thus λ=-1/5 or 1/10, with respective eigenfunctions Bxe^{-x} and Ce^{x/2}(x-3), using nonzero constants.
